idiom_name: NewClient(addr string, opts ...Option) with type Option func(*Config) and WithX constructors
implementation_notes: Go has no default arguments, no overloading and no inheritance, so the classic builder is not what the ecosystem uses: the constructor takes required values positionally and a variadic Option function type applies the optional ones (type Option func(*Config), or Option func(*T) error when an option can fail), after the constructor has installed the defaults in one place. Option values compose and can be stored, and adding a tenth WithX never breaks an existing call site - gRPC-Go (grpc.DialOption), zap and most AWS SDK v2 client constructors follow this shape. Keep the hand-written fluent builder for genuinely staged construction (query DSLs such as squirrel) or when Build() must validate the whole accumulated configuration and return an error.
pitfalls: An option that can fail cannot report the error through func(*Config): either give the option type an error return and stop at the first failure, or store the error in the config - otherwise a bad value is silently kept.
Options run in slice order after the defaults, so two options touching the same field make the last one win; document the ordering or reject conflicting combinations in the constructor.
Applying options straight to the half-built object (instead of a private config) exposes a partially initialised value to option code.

variants.name: Fluent builder struct (query DSLs, validating construction)
variants.idiom_name: NewBuilder(...) returning *Builder whose steps return the builder, plus Build() (*T, error)
variants.implementation_notes: The classic structure in Go is a builder struct with one pointer-receiver method per step returning the builder, plus a terminal Build() that validates the accumulated configuration and returns (*T, error) - the shape query builders and other DSLs use when the caller's chain is conditional. It reads un-idiomatically next to functional-options constructors and makes the builder part of the public API, so prefer it when validation needs the whole picture or the steps are genuinely sequential.
variants.code_sketch:
q := query.NewBuilder("users").
    Select("id", "email").
    Where("active = ?", true).
    OrderBy("name")
sql, args, err := q.Build()   // validates and returns the finished statement
pitfalls: Setters need pointer receivers (func (b *Builder) Where(...) *Builder); a value receiver silently mutates a copy and the step is lost.
A builder holds mutable scratch state, so it is single-use and not goroutine-safe: storing one in a struct and reusing it races or accumulates clauses.
